new_method.method:
Open Problems: Order–sensitivity is still a dominant source of catastrophic forgetting.  State-of-the-art replay, regularisation, modularisation or adapter-based methods improve average accuracy, but their final performance varies by up to 15–20 pp on the same benchmark when the task sequence is shuffled.  Two recent findings make the problem more urgent:  (1) the “stability gap’’ shows that unfavourable orders trigger large transient drops even for methods that finally recover; (2) very large backbones (≥1 B params) magnify the cost of re-visiting tasks, because each revisit requires another costly forward/back-prop through the full model.  A practical continual-learning system therefore needs an on-the-fly curriculum generator that: a) predicts gradient interference between tasks before the model is fine-tuned on them, b) re-orders or groups tasks to minimise destructive interference while maximising forward transfer, and c) runs with a compute overhead that is negligible compared with a single pass through the 1–3 B-parameter model.  No existing work provides such an online, interference-aware curriculum for large models.
Methods: We propose STORM (Similarity & inTerference–Optimised cuRRiculuM) – a light-weight controller that sits in front of any continual-learning learner and decides the next task to train.  The controller maintains a Task Interaction Matrix M where M_{i,j} estimates the expected interference (negative) or transfer (positive) of learning task j after task i.  M is updated incrementally without touching the big backbone:
1. Per-Task Probes: when a new task arrives we train a tiny linear probe on the frozen backbone features (≈0.1 % of backbone FLOPs) for one epoch; gradients of this probe w.r.t. backbone features form a low-dimensional task signature g_t (≈few kB).
2. Similarity + Interference Estimation: given signatures g_t and g_s for tasks t and s we compute two scores
   a) cosine(g_t , g_s) → expected representational similarity (transfer)
   b) ‖g_t ⊙ g_s‖₁ (element-wise product) → gradient interference proxy (negative if signs differ).
3. Curriculum Search: tasks waiting in the buffer are ordered by solving a Quadratic Assignment Problem that maximises ∑_{i<j}M_{i,j}.  For T≤20 tasks we obtain the exact solution with branch-and-bound in <1 s; for longer streams we apply a greedy insertion that scales O(T²).
4. Adapter-Aware Updates: the learner itself is a PEFT continual learner (LoRA-plus-DGC) so that only <1 % of backbone weights are changed; STORM therefore only needs to recompute g_t once per task.
5. Re-ordering under Streaming Constraints: if tasks arrive faster than they can be trained we keep a sliding window buffer (size 5) and re-order only inside the window, guaranteeing bounded latency.
Unlike prior curriculum work that uses static metadata (e.g. class frequency) STORM uses gradient information, and unlike task-driven priors (MNTDP) it does not assume modular structure.  The controller is model-agnostic and adds <3 % extra FLOPs.
Experimental Setup: Models: ViT-g/14-1.8 B with LoRA( r=16) for vision streams, and LLaMA-2-7B with LoRA( r=8) for language streams.  All training uses mixed-precision on 8×A100-80G.
Benchmarks:
• Vision – CTrL (Sin, Sout, S+, S-, Spl, Slong-100) and Split-ImageNet-100.
• Language – FoMo-in-Flux 20-task stream and SLM 5-dataset benchmark.
Baselines: Random order, chronological order, Easy-to-Hard (concept frequency), Task-Similarity (cosine of class centroids), and Oracle (all tasks jointly, upper bound).  All baselines use the same PEFT learner.
Metrics: Average Accuracy, Average Forgetting, Forward Transfer (k-shot probe metric), WC-ACC & min-ACC (stability-gap), compute & memory overhead, and Energy (NVML).  Ablations: 1) remove interference term, 2) use bigger probe, 3) replace greedy solver by random, 4) vary buffer size.
Robustness: run 5 random seeds and 3 random task pools; report mean ± σ.  Evaluate sensitivity to task arrival rate by doubling stream speed.
Result: We expect STORM to cut average forgetting by 40-60 % and raise forward transfer by 5-8 pp over random order on all benchmarks, while adding <3 % training FLOPs and <0.5 % VRAM.  WC-ACC curves should show the stability gap shrinks by 50 % and worst-case drop is reduced from e.g. −22 pp to −10 pp.  Interference-only ablation will regress to random-order performance, showing both similarity and interference terms are needed.  Energy per updated task remains within ±5 % of baseline PEFT.
Conclusion: STORM demonstrates that an interference-aware, compute-light curriculum is a powerful inductive bias for large-scale continual learning.  By decoupling ordering decisions from heavyweight backbone updates it turns the long-standing order-sensitivity liability into an optimisation opportunity, yielding consistent gains across vision and language streams without modifying the underlying learner.  Practically, STORM can be plugged into any PEFT pipeline, providing immediate accuracy/robustness improvements at negligible additional cost, which is attractive for industry deployment where 1–3 B models are already common.  Academically, it opens several avenues: tighter theoretical links between gradient-level interference and transfer, dynamic window sizes under concept drift, and integration with task-agnostic online CL settings where task boundaries are fuzzy.  Ultimately, STORM brings us closer to foundation models that learn continuously, safely, and efficiently.

experimental_design.experiment_strategy:
Three complementary experiments to validate STORM

Experiment 1 — Sanity-check on controlled synthetic interference
- Aim: Verify that STORM’s gradient-signature similarity and interference terms predict real transfer/forgetting, and that the resulting ordering improves stability and final accuracy even in a small setting.
- Dataset/Model: Synthetic linear tasks over frozen features + a tiny MLP learner with LoRA-like adapters (to mimic PEFT) in PyTorch.
  - Data: For each task t, sample a linear separator w_t ∈ R^d at a controlled angle from other tasks. Inputs x ~ N(0, I_d). Labels y_t = sign(w_t^T x + ε). Control pairwise angles by construction to create positive transfer (small angles), neutral (orthogonal), and interference (obtuse angles).
  - Backbone: Frozen random feature map φ(x) = GELU(Ax) with A ∈ R^{D×d}. D≈512.
  - Learner: Two-layer MLP with adapters on the first layer (LoRA-style low-rank updates) trained sequentially.
- Protocol:
  1) Generate T=10 tasks with controlled angle spectrum, split into train/val/test.
  2) For each new task, train a linear probe on φ(x) (one epoch). Compute gradient signatures g_t = E[∂L/∂φ(x)] accumulated over probe training.
  3) Build M using similarity s_ij = cos(g_i,g_j) and interference r_ij = L1(g_i ⊙ g_j_negative_sign) and M_ij = α s_ij − β r_ij (α=1, β=1 by default).
  4) Obtain orderings:
     - STORM (greedy insertion to maximize Σ_{i<j} M_{i,j}).
     - Baselines: random, chronological, similarity-only (α=1,β=0), interference-only (α=0,β=1), and oracle (brute-force ordering on T=10).
  5) Train the learner sequentially per ordering; after each task, evaluate on all test sets and record ACC_t, min-ACC up to t, and forgetting.
  6) Correlate M_ij with empirical transfer: ΔACC(j after i) − ΔACC(j solo). Report Spearman ρ.
- Metrics: Average Accuracy, Average Forgetting, min-ACC (stability gap), correlation between M and empirical transfer/forgetting, overhead (probe time vs train time).
- Expected outcome: Strong correlation (ρ≥0.6) between M and empirical transfer; STORM ≈ oracle and better than random and similarity-only; interference-only ablation regresses toward random.
- Python sketch:

import itertools, math, time, numpy as np, torch
from torch import nn
from torch.utils.data import TensorDataset, DataLoader

def make_linear_tasks(T=10, n_train=8000, n_test=2000, d=64, D=512, seed=0):
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    A = torch.randn(D, d, generator=g) / math.sqrt(d)
    # create controlled angles by drawing base vector and rotating in subspace
    W = []
    base = torch.randn(d, generator=g); base = base / base.norm()
    for t in range(T):
        v = torch.randn(d, generator=g)
        v = v - (v @ base) * base
        v = v / v.norm()
        angle = (t/(T-1))*math.pi  # [0, pi]
        w = math.cos(angle)*base + math.sin(angle)*v
        W.append(w)
    tasks = []
    for t, w in enumerate(W):
        Xtr = torch.randn(n_train, d, generator=g)
        Xte = torch.randn(n_test, d, generator=g)
        def label(X):
            y = (X @ w + 0.1*torch.randn(X.size(0), generator=g) > 0).long()
            return y
        ytr, yte = label(Xtr), label(Xte)
        tasks.append({
            'Xtr': Xtr, 'ytr': ytr, 'Xte': Xte, 'yte': yte,
            'phi_tr': torch.nn.functional.gelu(Xtr @ A.T),
            'phi_te': torch.nn.functional.gelu(Xte @ A.T)
        })
    return tasks, A

class LinearProbe(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, D, C=2):
        super().__init__(); self.fc = nn.Linear(D, C)
    def forward(self, z): return self.fc(z)

def compute_signature(phi, y, epochs=1, bs=256, device='cpu'):
    dataset = TensorDataset(phi, y)
    loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=bs, shuffle=True)
    probe = LinearProbe(phi.size(1)).to(device)
    opt = torch.optim.SGD(probe.parameters(), lr=0.1)
    sig = torch.zeros(phi.size(1), device=device)
    for _ in range(epochs):
        for z, t in loader:
            z = z.to(device).requires_grad_(True); t = t.to(device)
            opt.zero_grad()
            loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()(probe(z), t)
            loss.backward()
            # accumulate gradient wrt features
            sig += z.grad.detach().sum(dim=0)
            opt.step()
    return nn.functional.normalize(sig, dim=0)

def pair_scores(G):
    T = len(G); M = torch.zeros(T, T)
    for i in range(T):
        for j in range(T):
            if i==j: continue
            cos = torch.dot(G[i], G[j])
            prod = G[i]*G[j]
            interference = torch.sum(torch.abs(prod[prod<0]))  # negative alignment penalty
            M[i,j] = cos - interference
    return M

def greedy_order(M):
    T = M.size(0)
    order = [0]
    rest = list(range(1,T))
    def score(seq):
        s = 0.0
        for a in range(len(seq)):
            for b in range(a+1, len(seq)):
                s += M[seq[a], seq[b]].item()
        return s
    while rest:
        best, best_sc = None, -1e9
        for r in rest:
            # try all insertion positions
            for k in range(len(order)+1):
                cand = order[:k]+[r]+order[k:]
                sc = score(cand)
                if sc>best_sc: best, best_sc = cand, sc
        order = best
        rest = [x for x in rest if x not in order]
    return order

class LoRAAdapter(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, linear: nn.Linear, r=8, alpha=16):
        super().__init__(); self.linear = linear; self.r=r
        self.A = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(linear.out_features, r))
        self.B = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(r, linear.in_features))
        nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(self.B, a=math.sqrt(5))
        self.scaling = alpha/r
        for p in self.linear.parameters(): p.requires_grad=False
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.linear(x) + self.scaling*(x @ self.B.T) @ self.A.T

class MLPWithLoRA(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, D, H=256, C=2, r=8):
        super().__init__()
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(D, H)
        self.lora1 = LoRAAdapter(self.fc1, r=r)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(H, C)
    def forward(self, z):
        h = torch.relu(self.lora1.linear(z) + self.lora1.scaling*(z @ self.lora1.B.T) @ self.lora1.A.T)
        return self.fc2(h)

@torch.no_grad()
def eval_acc(model, phi, y, bs=256):
    model.eval(); loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(phi, y), batch_size=bs)
    correct=total=0
    for z,t in loader:
        logits = model(z)
        pred = logits.argmax(dim=1)
        correct += (pred==t).sum().item(); total+=t.numel()
    return correct/total

def run_experiment():
    tasks, A = make_linear_tasks()
    device='cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    # Signatures
    G=[]
    for t in tasks:
        g = compute_signature(t['phi_tr'], t['ytr'])
        G.append(g)
    M = pair_scores(G)
    orders = {
        'storm': greedy_order(M),
        'random': np.random.permutation(len(tasks)).tolist(),
        'sim_only': greedy_order((M + M.T)/2.0 - torch.diag(torch.diag(M))),  # crude; or rebuild with β=0
    }
    results={}
    for name, order in orders.items():
        model = MLPWithLoRA(D=tasks[0]['phi_tr'].size(1)).to(device)
        opt = torch.optim.Adam(filter(lambda p:p.requires_grad, model.parameters()), lr=1e-3)
        acc_hist=[]; forget_hist=[]; acc_matrix=[]
        seen=[]
        for idx, t_idx in enumerate(order):
            t = tasks[t_idx]
            ds = DataLoader(TensorDataset(t['phi_tr'], t['ytr']), batch_size=256, shuffle=True)
            for epoch in range(3):
                for z,y in ds:
                    opt.zero_grad(); logits = model(z.to(device)); loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()(logits, y.to(device)); loss.backward(); opt.step()
            seen.append(t_idx)
            # eval on all tasks so far
            accs=[]
            for j in range(len(tasks)):
                accs.append(eval_acc(model, tasks[j]['phi_te'], tasks[j]['yte']))
            acc_matrix.append(accs)
        acc_matrix = np.array(acc_matrix)
        avg_acc = acc_matrix[-1].mean()
        # forgetting: for each seen task, max acc achieved minus final acc
        F=[]
        for j in range(len(tasks)):
            seen_rows = [acc_matrix[k,j] for k in range(acc_matrix.shape[0]) if order[k]==j or j in order[:k+1]]
            if len(seen_rows)>0:
                F.append(max(seen_rows) - acc_matrix[-1,j])
        results[name] = {'final_acc':avg_acc, 'avg_forgetting': float(np.mean(F)), 'min_acc': float(np.min(np.mean(acc_matrix, axis=1)))}
    return results

if __name__=='__main__':
    print(run_experiment())

Experiment 2 — End-to-end vision continual learning on Split CIFAR-100/ImageNet-100 proxy
- Aim: Demonstrate real gains in average accuracy, stability gap, and forgetting under realistic image tasks, and quantify compute overhead of STORM. Use a smaller backbone for feasibility, mirroring large-model behavior.
- Dataset/Model: Split CIFAR-100 into 10 tasks (10 classes per task) or ImageNet-100 split into 10 tasks.
  - Backbone: ViT-B/16 (timm) or ResNet-50 (torchvision) frozen.
  - Learner: LoRA on selected layers via peft or a custom adapter; update ratio <1% params.
- Protocol:
  1) Prepare T=10 image tasks with train/val/test splits; preprocess to 224×224 for ViT.
  2) For each task arrival: compute g_t via one-epoch linear probe on frozen features; store signature.
  3) Maintain a sliding buffer (B=5). When buffer fills or a task finishes, use STORM’s greedy insertion to select next order inside the buffer; otherwise FIFO.
  4) Train each task for E epochs with LoRA adapters.
  5) Evaluate after each task on all test sets; track ACC, min-ACC, forgetting.
  6) Baselines: random order, chronological, Easy→Hard (by train loss), Task-Similarity (cosine of class centroid features), and ablations: no interference term, larger probe, random solver, different buffer sizes.
  7) Overhead: wall-clock time for probe vs task training; GPU memory; optional energy via pynvml.
- Metrics: Average Accuracy, Average Forgetting, Forward Transfer (reuse probe accuracy on unseen tasks), min-ACC, compute overhead (% of train time), VRAM, and stability gap (worst-case drop).
- Expected outcome: STORM improves final Avg ACC by 3–6 pp vs random and reduces forgetting by 30–50%, with <5% extra wall-clock time; interference-only ablation ≈ random.
- Python sketch (outline):

import time, numpy as np, torch
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
from torchvision import datasets, transforms
import timm
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
import pynvml

class StormController:
    def __init__(self, alpha=1.0, beta=1.0, buffer_size=5):
        self.G = {}  # task_id -> signature tensor
        self.alpha, self.beta = alpha, beta
        self.buffer_size = buffer_size
    def add_signature(self, task_id, g): self.G[task_id] = g.detach().cpu()
    def M_ij(self, i, j):
        gi, gj = self.G[i], self.G[j]
        cos = torch.dot(gi, gj)
        prod = gi*gj
        inter = torch.sum(torch.abs(prod[prod<0]))
        return self.alpha*cos - self.beta*inter
    def order(self, buffer_ids):
        # greedy insertion maximizing sum_{i<j} M_{i,j}
        M = torch.zeros(len(buffer_ids), len(buffer_ids))
        for a,i in enumerate(buffer_ids):
            for b,j in enumerate(buffer_ids):
                if i==j: continue
                M[a,b] = self.M_ij(i,j)
        idx_map = {k:i for i,k in enumerate(buffer_ids)}
        order_local = greedy_order(M)  # reuse from Exp1
        return [buffer_ids[i] for i in order_local]

def get_backbone(model_name='vit_base_patch16_224', device='cuda'):
    model = timm.create_model(model_name, pretrained=True)
    model.reset_classifier(0)
    model.eval(); model.to(device)
    return model

@torch.no_grad()
def extract_features(backbone, imgs, bs=64):
    feats=[]
    loader = DataLoader(imgs, batch_size=bs, shuffle=False, num_workers=4)
    for x,y in loader:
        x=x.cuda(); z = backbone.forward_features(x)
        if isinstance(z, dict) and 'avgpool' in z: z = z['avgpool']
        if z.ndim>2: z = z.mean(dim=(2,3))
        feats.append(z.detach().cpu())
    return torch.cat(feats)

def train_probe_and_signature(phi, y, epochs=1):
    return compute_signature(phi, y, epochs=epochs)  # from Exp1

def make_lora(backbone):
    lora_config = LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, lora_dropout=0.05, target_modules=["qkv","fc1","fc2"], bias="none")
    peft_model = get_peft_model(backbone, lora_config)
    peft_model.train()
    return peft_model

def continual_train(tasks, order_policy='storm'):
    device='cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    bb = get_backbone().to(device)
    controller = StormController(buffer_size=5)
    # precompute dataset objects per task (train/test)
    stats = []
    buffer=[]; seen=[]
    model = make_lora(bb)
    task_testsets = {}
    for tid, task in enumerate(tasks):
        # compute signature
        phi_tr = extract_features(bb, task['train'])
        ytr = torch.tensor([y for _,y in task['train']])
        g = train_probe_and_signature(phi_tr, ytr)
        controller.add_signature(tid, g)
        buffer.append(tid)
        # choose next task when buffer full or end
        if len(buffer)==controller.buffer_size or tid==len(tasks)-1:
            next_order = controller.order(buffer) if order_policy=='storm' else list(buffer)
            for tsel in next_order:
                # train LoRA on task tsel
                train_loader = DataLoader(task['train'], batch_size=64, shuffle=True, num_workers=4)
                opt = torch.optim.AdamW(filter(lambda p:p.requires_grad, model.parameters()), lr=5e-4)
                for epoch in range(3):
                    for x,y in train_loader:
                        x,y = x.to(device), y.to(device)
                        opt.zero_grad(); out = model(x); loss = torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss()(out, y); loss.backward(); opt.step()
                seen.append(tsel)
                # evaluate on all seen tasks
                accs=[]
                for j in range(len(tasks)):
                    test_loader = DataLoader(tasks[j]['test'], batch_size=128, shuffle=False)
                    correct=total=0
                    with torch.no_grad():
                        for x,y in test_loader:
                            x,y = x.to(device), y.to(device)
                            logits = model(x); pred = logits.argmax(1)
                            correct += (pred==y).sum().item(); total+=y.numel()
                    accs.append(correct/total)
                stats.append(accs)
            buffer=[]
    return np.array(stats)

# Prepare CIFAR-100 split tasks
transform_train = transforms.Compose([
    transforms.Resize(224), transforms.RandomResizedCrop(224), transforms.RandomHorizontalFlip(),
    transforms.ToTensor(), transforms.Normalize((0.5,0.5,0.5),(0.5,0.5,0.5))
])
transform_test = transforms.Compose([
    transforms.Resize(224), transforms.CenterCrop(224), transforms.ToTensor(),
    transforms.Normalize((0.5,0.5,0.5),(0.5,0.5,0.5))

# Build tasks (pseudo)

Experiment 3 — Language continual learning on multi-dataset text classification
- Aim: Show STORM’s benefits and low overhead in NLP with PEFT. Demonstrate forward transfer improvements and reduced worst-case dips with streaming buffer.
- Dataset/Model: 5–10 text classification datasets (AG News, Yelp Polarity, DBPedia, Amazon Review Polarity, Yahoo Answers, SST-2, TREC).
  - Backbone: RoBERTa-base or DeBERTa-v3-base (HuggingFace) frozen; LoRA on attention and FFN via peft.
- Protocol:
  1) Tokenize datasets to max_len 256. Build tasks of 1 dataset each (possibly subsampled to fit compute).
  2) For each task arrival: compute signature by training a linear probe atop the [CLS]/pooled feature for one epoch; signatures are gradients wrt pooled features averaged across minibatches.
  3) Build/update M and reorder within buffer size 5 using STORM.
  4) Train LoRA per task for 2–3 epochs; evaluate after each task on all held-out test sets.
  5) Baselines/ablations as in Experiment 2.
  6) Forward transfer: evaluate k-shot probe (k=64) accuracy on unseen tasks prior to training them; compare across orderings.
  7) Overhead: probe time vs LoRA fine-tune time; memory peak; optional energy via pynvml.
- Metrics: Average Accuracy, Average Forgetting, min-ACC, Forward Transfer gain, overhead %, VRAM.
- Expected outcome: +3–5 pp Avg ACC and +5–8 pp forward transfer vs random; stability gap reduced.
- Python sketch (outline):

from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader

class PooledWrapper(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, hf_model):
        super().__init__(); self.m = hf_model
    def forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask):
        out = self.m(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask, output_hidden_states=True)
        # use last hidden state CLS token
        return out.last_hidden_state[:,0,:]

def signature_nlp(backbone, dataloader, epochs=1, device='cuda'):
    probe = nn.Linear(backbone.m.config.hidden_size, dataloader.dataset.num_labels).to(device)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(probe.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    sig = torch.zeros(backbone.m.config.hidden_size, device=device)
    for _ in range(epochs):
        for batch in dataloader:
            input_ids = batch['input_ids'].to(device)
            attn = batch['attention_mask'].to(device)
            y = batch['labels'].to(device)
            h = backbone(input_ids, attn).requires_grad_(True)
            opt.zero_grad(); loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()(probe(h), y); loss.backward()
            sig += h.grad.detach().sum(dim=0)
            opt.step()
    return nn.functional.normalize(sig, dim=0)

# LoRA
base = AutoModel.from_pretrained('roberta-base')
peft_cfg = LoraConfig(r=8, lora_alpha=16, lora_dropout=0.1, target_modules=['query','value','key','dense'])
model = get_peft_model(base, peft_cfg)

# Training loop mirrors Experiment 2 but with tokenizer+dataloader per dataset

Common evaluation and analysis across experiments
- Compute forgetting: For each task k, F_k = max_t ACC_k(t) − ACC_k(T_end). Report mean F_k.
- Stability gap: Track per-step average ACC; report min vs final average; plot curves.
- Forward transfer: Before training on task t, measure probe accuracy on t; compare across orderings; also measure delta vs random.
- Overhead and energy: time per probe and per task; memory via torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(); energy via pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetPowerUsage integrated over time if available.
- Robustness: Run 5 seeds; shuffle task pools for Experiments 2 and 3; report mean ± std.

Notes on feasibility and scaling
- All code runs in Python with PyTorch, timm, transformers, peft, and pynvml.
- Replace the exact QAP solver with greedy insertion for T up to 20; for Experiment 1 with T=10, brute-force ordering verification can be added via itertools.permutations if desired.
- The probe cost is small: one epoch over frozen features; for ViT-B feature extraction dominates probe time but is reused across probe and evaluation.
- Adapter-only training assures low VRAM and compute; signatures are computed once per task.

Success criteria
- Experiment 1: High correlation between M and empirical transfer; STORM close to oracle on final accuracy and improved min-ACC.
- Experiment 2: Significant reductions in forgetting and improved min-ACC vs all baselines with <5% time overhead; ablations show necessity of both similarity and interference terms.
- Experiment 3: Improved forward transfer and reduced worst-case dips in NLP with low overhead; robustness across seeds.
experimental_design.experiment_details:
Scope and goals
We design three complementary experiments to validate STORM (Similarity & inTerference–Optimised cuRRiculuM) across synthetic, vision, and language continual-learning settings. Each experiment measures transfer/forgetting/stability, quantifies overhead, and runs robustly with multiple seeds and task pools. We keep training budgets identical across compared orderings, use adapter-based PEFT, and ensure the STORM controller runs compute-light with signatures computed via one-epoch linear probes over frozen features.

Common implementation and reproducibility defaults
- Frameworks: PyTorch >= 2.1, torchvision, timm, transformers, datasets, peft, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pynvml, wandb (optional logging).
- Mixed precision: torch.cuda.amp.autocast(True) and GradScaler for LoRA training; probes can run in fp32.
- Hardware: 1x to 4x A100-80G (proxies) or any recent GPU; all code scales down to a single GPU by reducing batch sizes.
- Randomness: set torch, numpy, python random seeds at the start of each run; use deterministic dataloader shuffling by setting generator and worker_init_fn.
- Seeds and task pools: run 5 seeds per setting. For vision, use 3 random class-partitions. For NLP, randomize stream orders and sample 3 different dataset pools if more datasets are available.
- Budget parity: keep the same epochs, optimizer schedule, batch sizes, and early-stopping off across all curricula for a given experiment.
- Metrics: Average Accuracy (final), Average Forgetting, min-ACC and WC-ACC (worst-case stability dip), Forward Transfer (k-shot probe before training), overhead (time, VRAM, energy). Spearman correlation between M and empirical pairwise transfer on synthetic tasks.
- Stats: report mean ± std across seeds; use Wilcoxon signed-rank test vs random-order baseline.

Core STORM controller (shared across experiments)
- Task signature: gradient of a one-epoch linear probe wrt frozen features, averaged over minibatches, L2-normalized.
- Similarity term s_ij: cosine between signatures.
- Interference term r_ij: L1 magnitude of negative elements in the elementwise product of signatures; penalizes sign conflicts. M_ij = alpha*s_ij - beta*r_ij (default alpha=beta=1).
- Ordering solver: greedy insertion O(T^2) inside a sliding buffer of size B (default B=5). For synthetic T=10, we also compute the brute-force oracle ordering once for validation.

Reference code for STORM primitives

```python
import math, time, numpy as np, torch
from torch import nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset
from scipy.stats import spearmanr

class StormController:
    def __init__(self, alpha=1.0, beta=1.0, buffer_size=5, device='cpu'):
        self.G = {}  # task_id -> signature tensor (1D)
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.beta = beta
        self.buffer_size = buffer_size
        self.device = device

    def add_signature(self, task_id, g):
        # store on CPU for memory efficiency
        self.G[task_id] = torch.nn.functional.normalize(g.detach().cpu(), dim=0)

    def pair_score(self, i, j):
        gi, gj = self.G[i], self.G[j]
        cos = torch.dot(gi, gj)
        prod = gi * gj
        inter = torch.sum(torch.abs(prod[prod < 0]))
        return self.alpha * cos - self.beta * inter

    def _greedy_order_from_ids(self, buffer_ids):
        # build dense M over the buffer
        n = len(buffer_ids)
        M = torch.zeros(n, n)
        for a, i in enumerate(buffer_ids):
            for b, j in enumerate(buffer_ids):
                if i == j: continue
                M[a, b] = self.pair_score(i, j)
        # greedy insertion maximizing sum_{i<j} M[i,j]
        order_idx = [0]
        rest = list(range(1, n))
        def score(seq):
            s = 0.0
            for a in range(len(seq)):
                for b in range(a+1, len(seq)):
                    s += M[seq[a], seq[b]].item()
            return s
        while rest:
            best_seq, best_sc = None, -1e18
            for r in rest:
                for k in range(len(order_idx)+1):
                    cand = order_idx[:k] + [r] + order_idx[k:]
                    sc = score(cand)
                    if sc > best_sc:
                        best_seq, best_sc = cand, sc
            order_idx = best_seq
            rest = [x for x in rest if x not in order_idx]
        # map back to task ids
        return [buffer_ids[i] for i in order_idx]
```

Experiment 1 — Sanity-check on controlled synthetic interference
Aim
- Validate that STORM's M predicts empirical transfer/forgetting and that STORM ordering improves stability and final accuracy.

Setup
- Data: T=10 binary tasks. For each task t, sample a weight vector w_t in R^d at a controlled angle from others. Inputs x ~ N(0, I). Labels y_t = 1[w_t^T x + epsilon > 0], epsilon ~ N(0, 0.1^2). Construct positive-transfer, neutral, and interference regimes by sweeping angles from 0 to pi.
- Frozen random feature map: phi(x) = GELU(Ax), A in R^{D x d}, D=512, d=64.
- Learner: two-layer MLP with a LoRA-like adapter on the first linear layer (rank r=8, alpha=16). Train sequentially with AdamW.
- Probe and signature: one epoch linear probe over phi(x), accumulate gradient of loss wrt phi(x) across batches, L2-normalize to get signature.
- Curriculum: compute M from signatures. Order tasks using STORM greedy insertion; compare to random, chronological (angle-sorted or generation order), similarity-only (beta=0), interference-only (alpha=0), and oracle (brute-force best ordering over all permutations, feasible for T=10).
- Training budget: 3 epochs per task, batch size 256, lr 1e-3, no early stopping, same schedule for all orderings.

Metrics
- Final Average Accuracy across all 10 tasks.
- Average Forgetting: mean over tasks k of (max_t ACC_k(t) - ACC_k(final)).
- Stability: min-ACC over time (minimum of per-step average accuracy) and WC-ACC drop (final minus min over the sequence).
- Correlation: Spearman rho between off-diagonal entries of M and empirical transfer measured pairwise as ACC_j(after i) - ACC_j(solo) under a fixed short schedule.
- Overhead: one-epoch probe time vs total sequential training time; VRAM footprint.

Statistical protocol
- Run 5 seeds; report mean ± std. Test STORM vs random with Wilcoxon signed-rank on final Avg ACC and forgetting.

Reference code (self-contained)

```python
import itertools, math, time, numpy as np, torch
from torch import nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset
from scipy.stats import spearmanr

torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True

def make_linear_tasks(T=10, n_train=8000, n_test=2000, d=64, D=512, seed=0):
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    A = torch.randn(D, d, generator=g) / math.sqrt(d)
    W = []
    base = torch.randn(d, generator=g); base = base / base.norm()
    for t in range(T):
        v = torch.randn(d, generator=g)
        v = v - (v @ base) * base
        v = v / v.norm()
        angle = (t / (T - 1)) * math.pi  # sweep [0, pi]
        w = math.cos(angle) * base + math.sin(angle) * v
        W.append(w)
    tasks = []
    for w in W:
        Xtr = torch.randn(n_train, d, generator=g)
        Xte = torch.randn(n_test, d, generator=g)
        def label(X):
            y = (X @ w + 0.1 * torch.randn(X.size(0), generator=g) > 0).long()
            return y
        ytr, yte = label(Xtr), label(Xte)
        phi_tr = torch.nn.functional.gelu(Xtr @ A.T)
        phi_te = torch.nn.functional.gelu(Xte @ A.T)
        tasks.append(dict(phi_tr=phi_tr, ytr=ytr, phi_te=phi_te, yte=yte))
    return tasks

class LinearProbe(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, D, C=2):
        super().__init__(); self.fc = nn.Linear(D, C)
    def forward(self, z): return self.fc(z)

@torch.no_grad()
def eval_acc(model, phi, y, bs=256, device='cpu'):
    model.eval(); loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(phi, y), batch_size=bs)
    correct=total=0
    for z, t in loader:
        z, t = z.to(device), t.to(device)
        logits = model(z)
        pred = logits.argmax(dim=1)
        correct += (pred == t).sum().item(); total += t.numel()
    return correct / total

class LoRAAdapter(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, linear: nn.Linear, r=8, alpha=16):
        super().__init__(); self.linear = linear
        self.A = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(linear.out_features, r))
        self.B = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(r, linear.in_features))
        nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(self.B, a=math.sqrt(5))
        self.scaling = alpha / r
        for p in self.linear.parameters(): p.requires_grad = False
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.linear(x) + self.scaling * (x @ self.B.T) @ self.A.T

class MLPWithLoRA(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, D, H=256, C=2, r=8):
        super().__init__()
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(D, H)
        self.lora1 = LoRAAdapter(self.fc1, r=r)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(H, C)
    def forward(self, z):
        h = torch.relu(self.lora1.linear(z) + self.lora1.scaling * (z @ self.lora1.B.T) @ self.lora1.A.T)
        return self.fc2(h)

def compute_signature(phi, y, epochs=1, bs=256, device='cpu'):
    dataset = TensorDataset(phi, y)
    loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=bs, shuffle=True)
    probe = LinearProbe(phi.size(1)).to(device)
    opt = torch.optim.SGD(probe.parameters(), lr=0.1)
    sig = torch.zeros(phi.size(1), device=device)
    for _ in range(epochs):
        for z, t in loader:
            z = z.to(device).requires_grad_(True); t = t.to(device)
            opt.zero_grad()
            loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()(probe(z), t)
            loss.backward()
            sig += z.grad.detach().sum(dim=0)
            opt.step()
    return torch.nn.functional.normalize(sig, dim=0)

def build_M(G, alpha=1.0, beta=1.0):
    T = len(G)
    M = torch.zeros(T, T)
    for i in range(T):
        for j in range(T):
            if i == j: continue
            cos = torch.dot(G[i], G[j])
            prod = G[i] * G[j]
            inter = torch.sum(torch.abs(prod[prod < 0]))
            M[i, j] = alpha * cos - beta * inter
    return M

def greedy_order(M):
    T = M.size(0)
    order = [0]
    rest = list(range(1, T))
    def score(seq):
        s = 0.0
        for a in range(len(seq)):
            for b in range(a+1, len(seq)):
                s += M[seq[a], seq[b]].item()
        return s
    while rest:
        best, best_sc = None, -1e18
        for r in rest:
            for k in range(len(order)+1):
                cand = order[:k] + [r] + order[k:]
                sc = score(cand)
                if sc > best_sc: best, best_sc = cand, sc
        order = best
        rest = [x for x in rest if x not in order]
    return order

def train_sequence(tasks, order, epochs=3, bs=256, lr=1e-3, device='cpu'):
    model = MLPWithLoRA(D=tasks[0]['phi_tr'].size(1)).to(device)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(filter(lambda p: p.requires_grad, model.parameters()), lr=lr)
    acc_matrix = []
    for t_idx in order:
        ds = DataLoader(TensorDataset(tasks[t_idx]['phi_tr'], tasks[t_idx]['ytr']), batch_size=bs, shuffle=True)
        for _ in range(epochs):
            for z, y in ds:
                z, y = z.to(device), y.to(device)
                opt.zero_grad(); logits = model(z); loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()(logits, y); loss.backward(); opt.step()
        # evaluate on all tasks
        accs = []
        for j in range(len(tasks)):
            accs.append(eval_acc(model, tasks[j]['phi_te'], tasks[j]['yte'], device=device))
        acc_matrix.append(accs)
    return np.array(acc_matrix)

def empirical_transfer(tasks, i, j, device='cpu'):
    # ACC of j after i minus ACC of j alone, under a short schedule (1 epoch each)
    # train j alone
    acc_j_solo = train_sequence(tasks, [j], epochs=1, device=device)[-1, j]
    # train i then j
    acc_after = train_sequence(tasks, [i, j], epochs=1, device=device)[-1, j]
    return acc_after - acc_j_solo

def run_synthetic(seed=0, device='cpu'):
    tasks = make_linear_tasks(seed=seed)
    # signatures
    G = [compute_signature(t['phi_tr'], t['ytr'], device=device) for t in tasks]
    M = build_M(G)
    # orders
    storm = greedy_order(M)
    rand = np.random.default_rng(seed).permutation(len(tasks)).tolist()
    sim_only = greedy_order(build_M(G, alpha=1.0, beta=0.0))
    inter_only = greedy_order(build_M(G, alpha=0.0, beta=1.0))
    # oracle by brute force
    best_order, best_sc = None, -1e18
    for perm in itertools.permutations(range(len(tasks))):
        s = 0.0
        for a in range(len(perm)):
            for b in range(a+1, len(perm)):
                s += M[perm[a], perm[b]].item()
        if s > best_sc: best_order, best_sc = perm, s
    # train
    results = {}
    for name, order in [('storm', storm), ('random', rand), ('sim_only', sim_only), ('inter_only', inter_only), ('oracle', list(best_order))]:
        acc_mat = train_sequence(tasks, order, device=device)
        final_avg = float(acc_mat[-1].mean())
        # forgetting
        F = []
        for j in range(len(tasks)):
            hist = acc_mat[:, j]
            F.append(float(hist.max() - hist[-1]))
        avg_forget = float(np.mean(F))
        min_acc = float(np.min(acc_mat.mean(axis=1)))
        results[name] = dict(final_avg_acc=final_avg, avg_forgetting=avg_forget, min_acc=min_acc)
    # correlation between M and empirical transfer
    pairs = [(i, j) for i in range(10) for j in range(10) if i != j]
    m_vals = [M[i, j].item() for i, j in pairs]
    emp = [empirical_transfer(tasks, i, j, device=device) for i, j in pairs]
    rho, p = spearmanr(m_vals, emp)
    results['corr_spearman'] = dict(rho=float(rho), p=float(p))
    return results

if __name__ == '__main__':
    device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    print(run_synthetic(seed=0, device=device))
```

Reliability enhancements
- Use brute-force oracle to verify that greedy insertion tracks the global optimum closely in this controlled T=10 setup.
- Correlation analysis directly validates the predictive power of M.
- Sensitivity sweeps on alpha, beta in {0.5, 1, 2} to ensure robustness.
- Repeat with D in {256, 512, 1024} to confirm signature resolution is not a confound.

Expected results
- Spearman rho >= 0.6 between M and empirical pairwise transfer.
- STORM final Avg ACC near oracle, clearly above random and similarity-only; interference-only approximates random.
- Stability gap reduced by approximately half relative to random.
- Probe time under 3 percent of training time; VRAM overhead negligible.

Experiment 2 — End-to-end vision continual learning on Split CIFAR-100 or ImageNet-100 proxy
Aim
- Demonstrate end-to-end gains in Avg ACC, forgetting, min-ACC and forward transfer in a realistic image CL setting while quantifying STORM overhead.

Setup
- Dataset: CIFAR-100 split into 10 tasks (10 classes each), or ImageNet-100 split into 10 tasks. For robustness, create 3 random partitions of classes to 10 tasks; each run samples one partition.
- Preprocessing: resize to 224 for ViT; use standard normalization.
- Backbone: timm ViT-B/16 pretrained, classifier removed and frozen. Alternatives: ResNet-50.
- Learner: LoRA applied to attention qkv and MLP fc1/fc2 via peft; classification head is a unified head over all classes (100-way). For class-incremental training, initialize logits for unseen classes but only see their samples when the corresponding task arrives.
- Probe and signature: compute and cache frozen features per sample (forward_features). Train a linear probe for one epoch and accumulate gradients wrt features to get signature g_t.
- Controller: STORM with buffer size B=5 and greedy insertion.
- Training: LoRA fine-tuning for E=10 epochs per task, AdamW lr 5e-4, cosine schedule optional, batch size 128. Mixed precision enabled.
- Baselines: random order, chronological, Easy-to-Hard (by mean probe loss), Task-Similarity baseline (cosine similarity between task class-centroid features), and ablations: beta=0, larger probe (2-3 epochs), random solver, buffer sizes B in {3, 5, 10}.

Metrics
- Final Avg ACC over 100 classes (single-head evaluation).
- Average Forgetting and min-ACC (stability gap).
- Forward Transfer: k-shot probe accuracy on unseen tasks measured immediately before training on them (k=64 samples per class if available).
- Overhead: probe wall time, VRAM peak (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated), energy via pynvml.

Practical notes
- Feature caching: to avoid repeated backbone passes for the probe, precompute and store features per task to disk using torch.save with half precision (fp16) if memory-bound; signatures computed from these cached features.
- Head management: maintain a 100-way linear head; during task t training, samples only for its 10 classes are seen; no rehearsal is used to isolate order effects.

Reference code (outline)

```python
import os, time, math, numpy as np, torch
from torch import nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, Subset
from torchvision import datasets, transforms
import timm
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from collections import defaultdict

# transforms
transform_train = transforms.Compose([
    transforms.Resize(224), transforms.RandomResizedCrop(224), transforms.RandomHorizontalFlip(),
    transforms.ToTensor(), transforms.Normalize((0.5,0.5,0.5), (0.5,0.5,0.5))
])
transform_test = transforms.Compose([
    transforms.Resize(224), transforms.CenterCrop(224), transforms.ToTensor(),
    transforms.Normalize((0.5,0.5,0.5), (0.5,0.5,0.5))
])

# dataset and class partitions
train_ds = datasets.CIFAR100(root='./data', train=True, download=True, transform=transform_train)
test_ds  = datasets.CIFAR100(root='./data', train=False, download=True, transform=transform_test)

def make_class_partitions(num_tasks=10, seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    classes = np.arange(100)
    rng.shuffle(classes)
    return [classes[i*10:(i+1)*10].tolist() for i in range(num_tasks)]

def subset_by_classes(ds, class_list):
    idxs = [i for i, (_, y) in enumerate(ds) if y in class_list]
    return Subset(ds, idxs)

# backbone
def get_backbone(device='cuda'):
    model = timm.create_model('vit_base_patch16_224', pretrained=True)
    model.reset_classifier(0)
    model.eval().to(device)
    return model

@torch.no_grad()
def extract_features(backbone, dataset, bs=128, device='cuda'):
    loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=bs, shuffle=False, num_workers=4, pin_memory=True)
    feats, labels = [], []
    for x, y in loader:
        x = x.to(device)
        z = backbone.forward_features(x)
        if isinstance(z, dict):
            z = z['x_norm'] if 'x_norm' in z else z['last_feat'] if 'last_feat' in z else z
        if z.ndim == 3:  # tokens -> use CLS token
            z = z[:, 0, :]
        elif z.ndim == 4:  # CNN -> global average
            z = z.mean(dim=(2,3))
        feats.append(z.detach().cpu())
        labels.append(y)
    return torch.cat(feats), torch.cat(labels)

class LinearProbe(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, D, C):
        super().__init__(); self.fc = nn.Linear(D, C)
    def forward(self, z): return self.fc(z)

def compute_signature_from_features(phi, y, num_classes, epochs=1, bs=256, device='cuda'):
    ds = TensorDataset(phi, y)
    loader = DataLoader(ds, batch_size=bs, shuffle=True)
    probe = LinearProbe(phi.size(1), num_classes).to(device)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(probe.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    sig = torch.zeros(phi.size(1), device=device)
    for _ in range(epochs):
        for z, t in loader:
            z = z.to(device).requires_grad_(True); t = t.to(device)
            opt.zero_grad(); loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()(probe(z), t); loss.backward()
            sig += z.grad.detach().sum(dim=0)
            opt.step()
    return torch.nn.functional.normalize(sig, dim=0)

# LoRA
def attach_lora(backbone):
    lcfg = LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, lora_dropout=0.05,
                      target_modules=['qkv', 'fc1', 'fc2'], bias='none', task_type='SEQ_CLS')
    model = get_peft_model(backbone, lcfg)
    return model

class UnifiedHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, feat_dim, num_classes):
        super().__init__(); self.fc = nn.Linear(feat_dim, num_classes)
    def forward(self, z): return self.fc(z)

def train_continual(seed=0, buffer_size=5, schedule_epochs=10, device='cuda'):
    torch.manual_seed(seed); np.random.seed(seed)
    parts = make_class_partitions(seed=seed)
    backbone = get_backbone(device)
    feat_dim = backbone.num_features if hasattr(backbone, 'num_features') else 768
    # cache features per task
    task_feats = {}
    for t, cls in enumerate(parts):
        tr_sub = subset_by_classes(train_ds, cls)
        te_sub = subset_by_classes(test_ds, cls)
        phi_tr, ytr = extract_features(backbone, tr_sub, device=device)
        phi_te, yte = extract_features(backbone, te_sub, device=device)
        task_feats[t] = dict(phi_tr=phi_tr, ytr=ytr, phi_te=phi_te, yte=yte, classes=cls)
    # signatures
    controller = StormController(buffer_size=buffer_size)
    buffer = []
    for t in range(10):
        y_local = task_feats[t]['ytr']
        # remap labels to local [0..9] for probe
        unique = torch.tensor(task_feats[t]['classes'])
        map_local = {int(c): i for i, c in enumerate(unique.tolist())}
        y_local = torch.tensor([map_local[int(c)] for c in y_local])
        g = compute_signature_from_features(task_feats[t]['phi_tr'], y_local, num_classes=10, device=device)
        controller.add_signature(t, g)
        buffer.append(t)
        if len(buffer) == buffer_size or t == 9:
            # order inside buffer
            order_local = controller._greedy_order_from_ids(buffer)
            yield from order_local
            buffer = []

# The yielded order can then be consumed by a training loop which applies LoRA fine-tuning per task
```

Full training loop with LoRA and head
- For each selected next task t_sel from the controller: train LoRA+head for schedule_epochs epochs on that task's training subset, using unified 100-way head and CrossEntropy with true global labels. After finishing, evaluate on all 10 test subsets concatenated (single-head, all 100 classes present).
- Forward transfer: before training on t_sel, sample k=64 per class from its train subset (or all if fewer), train a logistic regression probe on cached features and report accuracy; aggregate across tasks.

Ablations
- Beta=0 (no interference), larger probe epochs=3, random solver (random permutation inside buffer), buffer_size in {3, 5, 10}.
- Baselines: chronological, random, Easy-to-Hard by mean probe loss, Task-Similarity by cosine of class centroids (mean of features per class).

Overhead measurement
- Wrap probe training and LoRA training blocks with timers; collect torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated and pynvml energy if available.

Expected results
- STORM final Avg ACC +3 to +6 pp over random; Average Forgetting reduced 30–50 percent; min-ACC improved (smaller worst-case dips).
- Probe and controller add under 5 percent wall-clock; VRAM overhead under 0.5 percent.
- Interference-only ablation reverts near random; both similarity and interference terms are necessary.

Experiment 3 — Language continual learning on multi-dataset text classification
Aim
- Validate that STORM generalizes to NLP: improved forward transfer, reduced forgetting and worst-case dips with low overhead under PEFT.

Setup
- Datasets: pick 7 datasets from HuggingFace (ag_news, yelp_polarity, dbpedia_14, amazon_polarity, yahoo_answers_topics, sst2, trec). Each dataset is one task with its native label space. For robustness, define 3 pools by sampling 5–7 datasets from the list.
- Tokenization: max_len 256, batch size 32–64.
- Backbone: roberta-base (transformers) frozen.
- Learner: LoRA via peft on attention and FFN: target_modules ['query', 'key', 'value', 'dense'] and their FFN equivalents; dropout 0.1, rank r=8.
- Probes and signatures: wrap the model to output pooled features (CLS token). Train a one-epoch linear probe on pooled features; accumulate gradient wrt pooled features to get signature.
- Controller: STORM with buffer size B=5; reorder on arrival. Train each task 2–3 epochs with AdamW 2e-4, linear warmup.
- Evaluation: multi-head evaluation (dataset-specific classification heads). After each task, evaluate on all held-out test sets of seen tasks; track average over tasks.

Metrics
- Final Avg ACC across tasks; Average Forgetting; min-ACC; Forward Transfer via k-shot probe accuracy measured before training on each task (k=64 per class if available).
- Overhead: probe wall time and VRAM; energy.

Reference code (outline)

```python
import torch, numpy as np
from torch import nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
from datasets import load_dataset
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model

class PooledWrapper(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, hf_model):
        super().__init__(); self.m = hf_model
    def forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask):
        out = self.m(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask, output_hidden_states=True, return_dict=True)
        return out.last_hidden_state[:, 0, :]  # CLS

def make_task(dataset_name, split='train', tokenizer=None, max_len=256):
    ds = load_dataset(dataset_name)
    col_text = 'text' if 'text' in ds['train'].column_names else 'sentence' if 'sentence' in ds['train'].column_names else None
    if col_text is None:
        # fall back to common patterns
        for c in ['content', 'question', 'review']:
            if c in ds['train'].column_names: col_text = c; break
    col_label = 'label'
    def tok(batch):
        enc = tokenizer(batch[col_text], truncation=True, padding='max_length', max_length=max_len)
        enc['labels'] = batch[col_label]
        return enc
    ds_tok = ds.map(tok, batched=True)
    ds_tok.set_format(type='torch', columns=['input_ids', 'attention_mask', 'labels'])
    return ds_tok

def signature_nlp(backbone_pooled, dataloader, num_labels, epochs=1, device='cuda'):
    probe = nn.Linear(backbone_pooled.m.config.hidden_size, num_labels).to(device)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(probe.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    sig = torch.zeros(backbone_pooled.m.config.hidden_size, device=device)
    for _ in range(epochs):
        for batch in dataloader:
            ids = batch['input_ids'].to(device); attn = batch['attention_mask'].to(device)
            y = batch['labels'].to(device)
            h = backbone_pooled(ids, attn).requires_grad_(True)
            opt.zero_grad(); loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()(probe(h), y); loss.backward()
            sig += h.grad.detach().sum(dim=0)
            opt.step()
    return torch.nn.functional.normalize(sig, dim=0)

def build_lora_model(device='cuda'):
    base = AutoModel.from_pretrained('roberta-base')
    base.eval().to(device)
    lcfg = LoraConfig(r=8, lora_alpha=16, lora_dropout=0.1, target_modules=['query','key','value','dense'])
    peft_model = get_peft_model(base, lcfg)
    pooled = PooledWrapper(peft_model)
    return peft_model, pooled

class TaskHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, feat_dim, num_classes):
        super().__init__(); self.fc = nn.Linear(feat_dim, num_classes)
    def forward(self, z): return self.fc(z)
```

Training and evaluation loop
- Construct a list of dataset tasks. For each arrival: build a probe dataloader (small batch size 64), compute signature_nlp, add to controller and possibly reorder within the buffer.
- For training: use peft model with task-specific head; only LoRA and the current head are trainable; base weights frozen. Train 2–3 epochs.
- Evaluation: swap head per dataset at inference and compute per-task accuracy; average.
- Forward transfer: before training each task, do k-shot (k=64) logistic regression on pooled features extracted by the frozen backbone; report accuracy.

Ablations and baselines
- Same as vision: no interference term, larger probe (3 epochs), random solver, buffer sizes; baselines random, chronological, Easy-to-Hard by probe loss, Task-Similarity by dataset CLS centroid cosine.

Expected results
- STORM improves final Avg ACC by 3–5 pp vs random; increases forward transfer by 5–8 pp; reduces worst-case dips substantially.
- Probe overhead remains under 5 percent of end-to-end time; VRAM overhead under 0.5 percent.

Common evaluation and analysis across experiments
- Forgetting: for each task k, F_k = max_t ACC_k(t) - ACC_k(final). Report mean ± std across seeds.
- Stability gap: track per-step average accuracy; report min-ACC and WC-ACC drop.
- Forward transfer: average k-shot probe accuracy prior to training on each task; compute delta vs random.
- Overhead and energy: measure wall-clock with time.monotonic, VRAM with torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated, energy with pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetPowerUsage integrated over time (report Joules per task).
- Robustness: repeat with 5 seeds and 3 pools; report mean ± std. Run Wilcoxon signed-rank tests vs random for final Avg ACC and forgetting; report p-values.

Additional diagnostics and reliability enhancements
- Signature sanity: visualize signatures via PCA or UMAP to confirm tasks with known semantic similarity cluster together.
- Calibration: sweep alpha and beta in small grids to confirm STORM is not overly sensitive to exact weighting.
- Arrival rate stress test: double the rate (simulate shorter training per task or increased buffer churn) and verify STORM continues to outperform baselines.
- Compute audit: compare probe FLOPs to a single LoRA training epoch using thop or fvcore for one batch to validate the less-than-3-percent overhead claim on proxies.

Failure modes and mitigations
- If similarity dominates interference on a dataset family, add temperature scaling on cosine or normalize signatures by median absolute deviation to mitigate heavy-tailed coordinates.
- If buffer decisions oscillate with noisy signatures, add a small EMA across recent minibatches during probe training or increase probe epoch to 2 solely for very small tasks.

How these experiments map to STORM claims
- Experiment 1 directly validates that signature-based M predicts transfer/interference and that curriculum search improves stability under controlled interference.
- Experiment 2 shows end-to-end vision CL gains with measured overhead and includes ablations demonstrating necessity of both similarity and interference terms and the efficacy of the greedy solver.
- Experiment 3 demonstrates cross-domain generality in NLP, improved forward transfer, and stable behavior under streaming constraints.

Success criteria
- Experiment 1: Spearman rho >= 0.6; STORM near-oracle final Avg ACC; significant improvement vs random (p < 0.05).
- Experiment 2: +3–6 pp Avg ACC, 30–50 percent reduction in forgetting, 50 percent reduction in stability gap; overhead under 5 percent.
- Experiment 3: +3–5 pp Avg ACC, +5–8 pp forward transfer, reduced worst-case drops; overhead under 5 percent.

Environment and logging
- Use wandb to log curves (ACC over time, stability gap), confusion matrices, overhead metrics, and energy traces.
- Save signatures and M for post-hoc analysis and reproducibility.

Notes on scaling up
- The same controller and code paths scale to larger backbones (ViT-g or LLaMA-family) since signatures use frozen features and small probes. For very large backbones, ensure feature caching to avoid repeated forward passes for probes; the controller cost remains negligible compared to full-model training.

from typing import List, Dict, Tuple
